In-app help of the MAVILERA RISC-V Laboratory, written for the application (spec W-D20); shown by the Help dialog (src/ui/help-dialog.js). The detailed documentation is content/help/docs/.

blocks.p: The MAVILERA RISC-V Laboratory runs RISC-V programs in your browser and shows how a processor executes them. Nothing is installed and nothing is uploaded.

ol: Type a program in the editor, or open one from Templates in the toolbar: short programs that each show one idea, with a note at the top on what to try.
Press Assemble (Ctrl+Enter). Errors are marked in the editor and explained in the console, with a hint.
Step through the program with Step (F10) and Step back (Shift+F10), or run it with Run (F5).
Watch the registers, memory and counters change. The last register written is marked ◆.
Switch to a processor view (Single-cycle, Multicycle, Pipelined) to see the same program on a datapath, one clock cycle at a time.

blocks.p: A program ends with the system call exit (li a7, 93 and ecall, with the exit code in a0) or with the pseudo-instruction halt, a jump to itself. The processor views stop at halt.

dl: The instruction-level simulator for RV32I and the M extension: editor, listing with machine words in hexadecimal and binary, instruction inspector, registers, call stack, counters, memory and console.

A processor that executes every instruction in one clock cycle. The paths the instruction uses are highlighted on the datapath; the Control tab shows the decoders, the Timing tab the critical paths and the clock period.
A processor that takes several shorter cycles per instruction, steered by a state machine. Show the datapath or the state diagram; Instruction ▶ runs all cycles of one instruction (F11).

A five-stage pipeline (IF, ID, EX, MEM, WB) with forwarding, load-use stalls, flushes and an optional branch predictor. The hazard unit can be set from none to complete to see what each part does. The pipeline diagram shows every instruction in every cycle.
In each processor view, the Waveforms tab draws chosen signals over the clock cycles run so far, as a timing diagram; select a cycle to go to it. The axis orders cycles; it is not hardware timing.
Runs the program of the editor to its halt on all three processors and tabulates instructions, cycles, CPI, clock period, execution time and speed-up, with illustrative delays.

blocks.p: The processor views implement a subset of RV32I (no byte or half-word loads and stores, no M extension) and have small memories. Use the ISA view for anything else.

ul: Assembly: the RV32I and M instructions, pseudo-instructions such as li, la, mv, j, call, ret, beqz and halt, and the directives .text .data .rodata .bss .word .half .byte .ascii .asciz .string .space .align .balign .equ .set.
System calls: a7 = 93 exits with the code in a0; a7 = 64 writes a2 bytes from the address in a1 to the console (a0 = 1).
C: choose C under Language. A teaching subset is compiled one statement at a time, in a plain or a register translation; point at a line on either side to see its counterpart.
GCC output: open a .s file made with gcc -S; it is adapted for the simulator and the changes are listed.
Point at an instruction in the editor for what it does; completion suggests mnemonics and registers.
Breakpoints: click a line number in the editor or an address in the listing (B on a row).
Watchpoints: tick a register's eye to stop when it is written; double-click a memory word, or use Watch, to stop when that word is written.
Step back undoes one step at a time, back to the start of the run (the oldest steps of a very long run are dropped, with a message).
Step over runs a call to its return; Step out runs to the return of the current procedure; Run to cursor stops at the editor's line.
The calling-convention check reports faults in the console, such as a procedure that returns with a register changed that it must keep.

The uninitialised-value check reports, in the console, a register read before anything wrote it, or a stack word loaded before anything stored it. It is the simulator's own check; saving ra or s0–s11 in a prologue is not reported.
A run that does not halt stops after a large number of instructions and says where it is looping.

dl: Step / step back (in a processor view, one clock cycle)
Step over / step out (in the multicycle view, one instruction)
Leave the editor (Tab inside it indents)
In the listing: move, show the fields, set a breakpoint
Resize panes (Shift for larger steps; Enter restores)
Open its details in a processor view

ul: Your work is kept in this browser: after a refresh or a closed tab, the program, its file name, the cursor, breakpoints, watchpoints, loaded data and the step you had reached come back.
File ▸ Copy share link puts the program, the view and its settings into a link. They travel in the part after #, which the browser never sends to a server.
File ▸ Save program and settings… writes a .json file; File ▸ Open reads it back, and also .s and .c files.

Exports: memory images for $readmemh and binary, the listing, traces (JSON lines, CSV), golden dumps for testbenches and VCD waveforms of the processor signals. The drawings export as SVG or PNG from Display.

Exercises: File ▸ Exercise… lists practice exercises written for MAVILERA, each with a starter program; a teacher's exercise file opens with File ▸ Open. Run the tests checks your program and shows expected against actual for each. No solutions are included.
File ▸ Data in and out… loads a CSV or binary file into a data array before a run, and saves a memory range.

blocks.p: Every computation runs in your browser. MAVILERA has no account, sends no telemetry and uploads nothing. After a first visit the hosted version also opens without a network connection, and a single-file version can be downloaded for computers that have none.

dl: The calling convention: which registers carry arguments and results, and which a procedure must keep (s0–s11, sp).
The time of one clock cycle, set by the slowest path that must finish within it.
Cycles per instruction: clock cycles divided by instructions completed.
An output of the control unit that sets a multiplexer, enables a write or selects an ALU operation.
The registers, memories, ALU, adders and multiplexers that hold and move data.
Discarding instructions fetched on the wrong path after a jump or a mispredicted branch.
Passing a result to a later instruction before it is written to the register file.
A situation in a pipeline where the next instruction cannot proceed as normal: a data dependence or a change of control flow.
A constant encoded in the instruction word.
The register between two pipeline stages (IF/ID, ID/EX, EX/MEM, MEM/WB) that carries an instruction's values to the next stage.
A convenient form that the assembler turns into one or more real instructions.
Holding an instruction in its stage for a cycle, for example until a loaded value is available.
